title: Sliding Window Median
description: Given an array of integers `nums` and a sliding window of size `k`, return the median of each window formatted to 1 decimal place.
input_format: First line contains `n` and `k`. Second line contains `n` integers.
hints: Maintain a sorted window of size k.
Calculate median from the middle element(s).
Remove the leaving element using binary search and insert the new element with `bisect.insort`.

starter_code.python:

reference_solution:
import sys, bisect
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[2:2+n]]
    window = sorted(nums[:k])
    out = []
    for i in range(k, n + 1):
        if k % 2 == 1: med = float(window[k // 2])
        else: med = (window[k // 2 - 1] + window[k // 2]) / 2.0
        out.append(f'{med:.1f}')
        if i < n:
            rem = nums[i - k]
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(window, rem)
            window.pop(idx)
            bisect.insort(window, nums[i])
    print(' '.join(out))
